# Original Wobbly Wars soldier

`soldier.glb` is an original low-poly, skinned glTF 2.0 model created for Little Big Arcade. It does not contain downloaded character artwork, textures, motion capture or third-party model parts.

**License:** CC0 1.0 Universal. The original geometry, materials and animation data in this asset are dedicated to the public domain; reuse and modification are permitted without attribution. The generator is included at `scripts/generate-wars-rig.py`.

## Integration

- Coordinates: metres; +Y up, +Z forward, soles at Y = 0.025. Height including plume is 2.15 m; helmet top is 2.0 m. Use a right-handed Babylon scene to retain the authored forward direction.
- A single skinned mesh contains 1,872 triangles in nine material primitives. Materials are named `team`, `skin`, `boots`, `steel`, `gold`, `eyes`, `white`, `leather`, `plume`. Clone `team` for independent army colors. `plume` can also be recolored by team or class.
- The model uses custom tapered ring profiles, costume plates and face vertices. Its final artwork is not assembled from runtime default mesh primitives.
- The skin has 14 named joints. All vertices have valid normalized skin weights. The bind pose has arms relaxed downward and both feet on the floor.
- Embedded `Idle` (2 s, breathing) and `Walk` (0.8 s, arms/legs) clips loop. Combat can blend or replace local joint rotations; do not keep the `Walk` group running while the unit is stationary.
- Weapon attachments use `handR`/`handL` wrist joints at local `(0, -0.05, 0.015)`, with the per-weapon mount rotation/pivot from `wars3d-weapons.js`. Do not attach new equipment directly to a forearm.

| Joint | Parent | Global bind position |
|---|---|---|
| root | — | 0, 0, 0 |
| hips | root | 0, 0.85, 0 |
| spine | hips | 0, 1.15, 0 |
| head | spine | 0, 1.55, 0 |
| armL | spine | -0.34, 1.35, 0 |
| foreL | armL | -0.38, 1.07, 0 |
| handL | foreL | -0.38, 0.78, 0 |
| armR | spine | 0.34, 1.35, 0 |
| foreR | armR | 0.38, 1.07, 0 |
| handR | foreR | 0.38, 0.78, 0 |
| legL | hips | -0.15, 0.85, 0 |
| shinL | legL | -0.15, 0.45, 0 |
| legR | hips | 0.15, 0.85, 0 |
| shinR | legR | 0.15, 0.45, 0 |

The generator checks finite positions/normals, normalized weights, joint ranges and binary buffer bounds. Browser import, visual animation and physical grounding still require runtime testing in the integrating scene.

## Original cavalry and artillery props

`pony.glb`, `dragon.glb` and `cannon.glb` are original articulated mesh assets generated by `scripts/generate-wars-props.py`, also dedicated under CC0 1.0 Universal. They use no external art or textures. Each mesh uses custom-authored loft profiles and polygon plates, with Y up and +Z forward. Named child mesh nodes allow rigid-part animation without a second skin.

| Asset | Triangles | Dimensions and attachment |
|---|---:|---|
| pony.glb | 816 | 0.71 m wide, 1.50 m high, 1.90 m long; saddle top near `(0, 1.09, -0.12)`. Friendly face, ears, mane, tail, team saddle blanket and four legs. |
| dragon.glb | 840 | 1.38 m wide with wings, 1.45 m high, 2.15 m long; saddle top near `(0, 1.08, -0.13)`. Faceted leaf wings, expressive eyes, curved tail, horns and team blanket. |
| cannon.glb | 754 | 1.02 m wide, 1.05 m high, 1.25 m long; muzzle at `(0, 0.785, 0.71)`. Wood carriage, steel-rimmed wheels, brass barrel bands and dark recessed bore. |

All props expose a `team` material for army color selection. Use the actual cannon muzzle coordinate for projectiles. Mount bodies stay under the rider root while their named legs and wings can move independently; these are rigid joint animations rather than deforming skins.

### Prop pivots and animation

Every GLB has a root named for the asset and a `body` child at `(0, 0, 0)`. The articulated parts are root siblings of `body`. Geometry is expressed relative to the named node's pivot, so the supplied rest translations preserve the original assembled silhouette exactly. Rotate legs around local X using distance-travelled gait phases; reset their rotations to zero when stationary. Cannon wheels rotate about local X with angle = distance / wheel radius (approximately 0.32 m). Dragon wings rotate around local Z with opposite signs.

| Asset | Node | Rest translation / pivot (m) |
|---|---|---|
| pony | legFL | -0.22, 0.60, 0.32 |
| pony | legFR | 0.22, 0.60, 0.32 |
| pony | legBL | -0.22, 0.60, -0.50 |
| pony | legBR | 0.22, 0.60, -0.50 |
| dragon | legFL | -0.23, 0.60, 0.32 |
| dragon | legFR | 0.23, 0.60, 0.32 |
| dragon | legBL | -0.23, 0.60, -0.49 |
| dragon | legBR | 0.23, 0.60, -0.49 |
| dragon | wingL | -0.19, 0.87, -0.20 |
| dragon | wingR | 0.19, 0.87, -0.20 |
| cannon | wheelL | -0.43, 0.325, -0.18 |
| cannon | wheelR | 0.43, 0.325, -0.18 |

Prop file sizes after articulation: pony 67,388 bytes; dragon 72,360 bytes; cannon 61,212 bytes. Triangle counts are unchanged.

## Wrist/grip correction (6.0.3)

The soldier now has fourteen joints: original body/limb joints plus independently weighted `handL`/`handR` wrists. Forearm pivots were moved to the elbows while recomputed inverse bind matrices preserve the rest mesh. `scripts/upgrade-wars-hands.mjs` documents/reproduces the upgrade from the original twelve-joint asset and is idempotent on this file. Weapon shapes and per-class grips are authored in `wars3d-equipment.js` / `wars3d-weapons.js`; no imported asset license changed.

## Arm reach and body clearance (6.0.4)

The original .204 m upper arm + .21 m forearm could not reach several two-handed poses in front of the .57 m wide torso. Reproduce the current asset by running `generate-wars-rig.py`, `upgrade-wars-hands.mjs`, then `fit-wars-arm-reach.mjs`. The last script fits the existing sleeve/forearm vertices, normals, elbow/wrist translations and inverse bind matrices to .283 m upper arms + .29 m forearms. Wrist weights, face, costume, colors, triangle count, dimensions of the torso and CC0 license remain. The script is a no-op after the revision marker is present.

The game uses the deterministic custom pose callback and stops embedded clips. Use `SOLDIER_BIND` to verify this current bind before authoring animations. Outward elbow guidance and carry/draw/strike trajectories are in `wars3d-poses.js`; do not move shoulders outward or stretch bones at runtime to hide a pose error. Dense tests validate actual skinned distal arm vertices against the torso core; the sleeve/pauldron seam remains intentionally overlapped.
